documents.title: Regulations Governing Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.) Degrees
documents.department: Office of Sponsored Research and Innovation
retrieval_signals: full time to part time PhD conversion
documents.content:
1. PURPOSE AND STATUTORY GOVERNANCE
These regulations govern the admission, enrollment, supervisory assignment, curriculum credit requirements, progress milestones, comprehensive examination, and thesis evaluation procedures for candidates registered for the Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.) degree at Demo University.

2. ENROLLMENT MODES AND DEGREE DURATION
2.1 Enrollment Categories: Candidates are admitted under Full-Time (FT) scholar status (supported by institutional fellowships or external sponsored project grants) or Part-Time status (for working professionals and in-service faculty).
- Entity Disambiguation: Full-Time (FT) doctoral enrollment must not be confused with student Field Trips (FT under ACAD-SOP-008).
2.2 Program Duration: The standard minimum doctoral duration is four (4) academic years (8 semesters). In accordance with university academic regulations, the maximum allowable period for thesis submission is N + 2 years (a total ceiling of six years from initial registration).

3. DOCTORAL COURSEWORK AND ACADEMIC BENCHMARKS (PROG-PHD-ENG)
3.1 Mandatory Credit Load: Every registered research scholar must earn a minimum of fourteen (14) graduate-level coursework credits:
- RES801: Research Methodology and Quantitative Analysis (Core, 4 Credits)
- RES802: Research and Publication Ethics (Core, 2 Credits)
- Departmental Advanced Technical Electives (8 Credits)
3.2 Minimum Grade Standard: Scholars must attain a minimum Cumulative Grade Point Average (CGPA) of 7.00 across completed coursework subjects before they are permitted to attempt the comprehensive examination.

4. DOCTORAL COMMITTEE (DC) AND COMPREHENSIVE ASSESSMENT
4.1 Committee Constitution: Within sixty (60) days of enrollment, the Dean of Research constitutes a dedicated Doctoral Committee (DC) comprising the Research Supervisor (Convener), Head of Department or nominee, two senior internal faculty experts, and one approved external subject specialist.
- Cross-Domain Disambiguation Note: Doctoral Committee (DC) under DEPT-RES must not be confused with the Disciplinary Committee (DC under DEPT-SW / STU-POL-005) or the Direct Current Hardware Laboratory (DC under DEPT-ECE / ECE-LAB-002).
4.2 Comprehensive Examination: Upon finishing prescribed coursework, the scholar must pass a written and oral comprehensive examination administered by the DC to assess foundational mastery in the research domain.

5. THESIS SUBMISSION AND DEFENSE
Following successful completion of semi-annual progress reviews (RES-POL-002), mandatory publication requirements, and certified plagiarism verification under RES-ETH-001, the scholar presents a public pre-synopsis colloquium. Upon DC endorsement, the final Ph.D. thesis is dispatched to two independent external evaluators for blind adjudication, culminating in an open oral defense viva voce.

documents.title: Doctoral Committee Progress Report (PR) Submission Guidelines
documents.department: Office of Sponsored Research and Innovation
documents.content:
1. PURPOSE AND INSTITUTIONAL MANDATE
This guideline defines the scheduling, submission requirements, evaluation rubrics, and administrative recording protocols for the mandatory semi-annual Progress Report (PR) presentations required of all doctoral scholars at Demo University.

2. DEFINITION AND CONTROLLED ENTITY DISAMBIGUATION
2.1 Progress Report (PR): Refers strictly to the formal semi-annual milestone documentation and presentation evaluated by a scholar's Doctoral Committee (DC) to audit research trajectory, lab deliverables, and fellowship eligibility.
- Cross-Domain Disambiguation Note: Progress Report (PR) under DEPT-RES must not be confused with Public Relations (PR under Admissions & Media / ADM-MED-001).

3. SEMI-ANNUAL REVIEW CYCLES AND WORKFLOW (REL-014)
3.1 Review Windows: Formal doctoral progress reviews are executed twice per academic calendar year:
- Odd Semester Cycle: Scheduled during June–July.
- Even Semester Cycle: Scheduled during December–January.
3.2 Submission Workflow on ResTrack:
- Step 1: The research scholar compiles the standardized PR dossier detailing literature surveys, experimental results, simulation data, chapter drafts, and publication manuscripts.
- Step 2: The Research Supervisor reviews, endorses, and submits the dossier via ResTrack Portal at least ten (10) calendar days prior to the committee meeting.
- Step 3: The Doctoral Committee convenes for an oral presentation and technical defense by the candidate.
- Step 4: The DC records formal evaluations using institutional rubrics ('Satisfactory' or 'Unsatisfactory') and uploads signed review minutes to ResTrack.

4. LINKAGE TO FELLOWSHIP DISBURSEMENT AND ACADEMIC CONTINUATION
4.1 Fellowship Authorization: Under REL-014, the release of monthly institutional research stipends and funded project fellowships is strictly contingent upon a validated 'Satisfactory' rating endorsed by the DC and ratified by the Dean of Research and Innovation.
4.2 Unsatisfactory Progress Sanction: An 'Unsatisfactory' evaluation results in immediate withholding of the monthly fellowship. Two consecutive 'Unsatisfactory' ratings warrant formal review by the Dean of Research and may result in the termination of doctoral registration.

documents.content:
1. PURPOSE AND APPLICABILITY
This policy establishes the appointment criteria, recruitment workflows, compensation guidelines, leave entitlements, and monthly fellowship release protocols for Research Assistants (RAs) and project staff appointed under externally sponsored research grants and institutional doctoral schemes.

2. DEFINITIONS AND CONTROLLED ENTITY DISAMBIGUATION
2.1 Research Assistant (RA): Refers strictly to a qualified postgraduate scholar or project engineer formally contracted under a sponsored research project to conduct experimental investigations, data analysis, and software development.
- Cross-Domain Disambiguation Note: Research Assistant (RA under DEPT-RES / ROLE-RA-RES) must not be confused with a Resident Assistant (RA under DEPT-HSTL / HSTL-REG-004 / ROLE-RA-HOSTEL), who is a senior student resident assisting with hostel floor governance.
2.2 Principal Investigator (PI): The lead faculty researcher accountable for the technical execution, milestone compliance, and fiscal management of a funded research grant.

3. SELECTION AND APPOINTMENT PROCEDURES
3.1 Open Recruitment: RA vacancies funded by external agencies (DST, SERB, CSIR, industry partners) are advertised publicly on the university research portal. Candidates are evaluated by a Department Selection Committee chaired by the PI.
3.2 Eligibility Thresholds: Candidates must hold relevant undergraduate or postgraduate degrees in the specified engineering or scientific discipline with verified national qualification credentials (GATE, NET) or demonstrated academic excellence.

4. MONTHLY STIPEND RELEASE WORKFLOW (REL-014)
4.1 Multi-Department Workflow: Monthly stipend disbursement requires a three-tier institutional handoff:
- Step 1 (Attendance Certification): The Research Supervisor / PI certifies the scholar's monthly lab attendance and research deliverables in ResTrack by the 25th calendar day of each month.
- Step 2 (Dean of Research Audit): The Office of Sponsored Research verifies ongoing milestone compliance and signs off on the disbursement voucher.
- Step 3 (Finance Accounts Credit): The Finance and Accounts Office releases authorized stipend funds directly to the scholar's verified bank account via electronic NEFT by the 1st working day of the subsequent month.
4.2 Inquiries Regarding Delayed Stipends: Inquiries concerning delayed Ph.D. stipends must be routed through ResTrack to the Dean of Research (`REL-014`), not to the undergraduate student scholarship office (`REL-002`).

5. LEAVE ENTITLEMENTS AND DISCIPLINARY CODES
Appointed Research Assistants are entitled to thirty (30) days of annual casual/medical leave per full academic year, approved by the PI. Unauthorized absence exceeding seven (7) consecutive days triggers immediate stipend suspension and appointment review.

documents.content:
1. PURPOSE AND SCOPE
This policy defines the governance principles, ownership criteria, patent filing assistance, technology transfer mechanisms, and commercialization revenue distribution governing inventions, design patents, and software copyrights generated by faculty, scholars, and students at Demo University.

2. DEFINITIONS AND CONTROLLED ENTITY DISAMBIGUATION
2.1 Intellectual Property Rights (IPR): Refers strictly to legal protections (patents, designs, trademarks, and copyrights) safeguarding novel technological discoveries, algorithms, and industrial hardware innovations.
- Cross-Domain Disambiguation Note: Intellectual Property Rights (IPR) under DEPT-RES must not be confused with IP Routing (IPR under DEPT-CSE / CSE-CRS-304 computer networking lab).

3. OWNERSHIP PRINCIPLES
3.1 University-Assisted Research: Inventions developed using university laboratory facilities, central computing infrastructure, or internal seed grant funding are owned jointly by the individual inventors and Demo University Higher Education Trust.
3.2 Independent Student Inventions: Intellectual property developed by students purely during academic coursework or extracurricular hackathons without significant institutional funding remains the exclusive property of the student inventors.
3.3 Sponsored Project IP: Ownership of inventions emerging from externally sponsored projects is governed by the specific contractual agreement signed with the external sponsoring agency (DST, corporate partners).

4. PATENT FILING AND COMMERCIALIZATION WORKFLOW
4.1 Step 1 — Invention Disclosure: The inventor completes an electronic Invention Disclosure Form (IDF) on ResTrack Portal, outlining technical novelty and claims.
4.2 Step 2 — IPR Committee Evaluation: The University IPR Evaluation Committee assesses patentability, prior art, and commercial translation viability.
4.3 Step 3 — Institutional Sponsorship: For approved inventions, the university finances one hundred percent (100%) of patent attorney drafting, filing, and statutory prosecution expenses.
4.4 Step 4 — Royalty Revenue Sharing: Net licensing royalties or commercialization revenues are distributed as sixty percent (60%) to the inventor(s) and forty percent (40%) to the University Research & Innovation Fund.

documents.department: Office of Sponsored Research and Innovation

documents.content:
1. PURPOSE AND INCUBATION OBJECTIVE
This framework establishes the operational policies, admission criteria, physical facility access, and venture mentoring provided by the Centre for Innovation and Entrepreneurship (CIE), operating within the South Research & Engineering Hub at Demo University.

2. THREE-STAGE VENTURE INCUBATION LIFECYCLE
2.1 Stage 1 — Pre-Incubation (Ideation and Proof-of-Concept):
- Duration: Up to six (6) months.
- Offerings: Free shared desk space, access to CIE MakerSpace rapid prototyping units, and technical faculty mentorship.
2.2 Stage 2 — Formal Incubation (Venture Incorporation):
- Duration: Twelve (12) to twenty-four (24) months.
- Offerings: Dedicated private office suites in Faraday Tower, formal legal entity incorporation assistance, accounting guidance, and subsidized patent filing support under RES-POL-004.
2.3 Stage 3 — Acceleration & Seed Linkages:
- Offerings: Investor pitch demo days, venture capital networking, and institutional seed capital allocation under RES-INC-002.

3. GOVERNANCE AND APPLICATION ADMISSION
3.1 Evaluation Panel: Venture applications submitted through ResTrack Portal are scrutinized quarterly by the CIE Incubation Advisory Board based on technical innovation, intellectual property defensibility, and market commercial viability.
3.2 Code of Conduct: Incubated companies must adhere strictly to environmental safety norms, intellectual property ethics, and campus security regulations.

1. PURPOSE AND SCOPE
These guidelines define the application workflows, eligibility criteria, seed funding disbursement, and MakerSpace tool reservation protocols governing the pre-incubation phase of student-led technology startups at Demo University.

2. DEFINITIONS AND CONTROLLED ENTITY DISAMBIGUATION
2.1 Centre for Innovation and Entrepreneurship (CIE): Refers strictly to the university startup incubator, innovation hub, and rapid prototyping makerspace facility located in the South Research & Engineering Hub.
- Cross-Domain Disambiguation Note: Centre for Innovation and Entrepreneurship (CIE under DEPT-RES) must not be confused with Continuous Internal Evaluation (CIE under DEPT-EXAM / EXAM-GUI-001 sessional examination assessments).

3. MAKERSPACE FACILITY USAGE AND TOOL RESERVATION
3.1 Hardware Prototyping Inventory: Registered pre-incubation teams receive access to precision 3D additive printers, laser cutting instruments, PCB milling machines, and cloud GPU compute sandboxes (LabServer Forge).
3.2 Machine Slot Booking: Tool reservations must be logged on ResolveDesk under 'CIE MakerSpace Reservation' at least forty-eight (48) hours in advance. Operators must pass mandatory safety induction training.

4. UNIVERSITY SEED GRANTS
4.1 Micro-Seed Funding Allocation: Prototype teams exhibiting novel technical proof-of-concept may receive institutional micro-seed grants to cover component acquisition, electronic sensors, fabrication materials, and cloud server hosting.
4.2 Application and Review: Proposals are submitted via ResTrack Portal and evaluated by the CIE Pitch Evaluation Committee; disbursed grant expenditures are audited by the Finance and Accounts Office.

documents.title: Research Ethics, Academic Integrity, and Plagiarism Prevention Code
documents.department: Office of Sponsored Research and Innovation
roles: Chairperson of Research Ethics Review Board
documents.content:
1. PURPOSE AND ETHICAL MANDATE
This institutional code establishes the binding ethical standards, integrity expectations, plagiarism detection limits, and review board clearance workflows governing all scientific inquiry, doctoral dissertations, postgraduate theses, and scholarly publications produced at Demo University.

2. PLAGIARISM TOLERANCE THRESHOLDS AND THESIS CLEARANCE
2.1 Statutory Ten Percent (10%) Threshold: In accordance with university academic regulations and national research integrity norms, the maximum permissible textual similarity index for all Ph.D. theses and M.Tech dissertations is strictly ten percent (<= 10%), excluding bibliography, mathematical equations, and standard institutional affiliations.
2.2 Mandatory Verification Protocol: All thesis manuscripts must be submitted to the Plagiarism & Thesis Verification Unit at the Valmiki Central Library for formal scanning using Turnitin / E-Shodh Hub prior to final submission (LIB-POL-004). An official, digitally signed Similarity Clearance Certificate must accompany every submitted thesis.

3. RESEARCH ETHICS REVIEW BOARD (RERB) CLEARANCE
3.1 Mandatory Ethical Approval: Experimental research involving human participants, private personal data, biometric surveillance, or animal specimens requires formal advance clearance from the Research Ethics Review Board (RERB).
3.2 Protocol Submission: Researchers must upload experimental consent forms, participant privacy safeguards, and risk-mitigation plans on ResTrack Portal prior to commencing clinical or field investigations.

4. SCHOLARLY INTEGRITY BREACHES AND SANCTIONS
Fabrication of experimental results, data falsification, duplicate publication, ghost authorship, or intentional plagiarism exceeding statutory limits constitutes severe scientific malpractice. Verified infractions result in immediate thesis rejection, revocation of research fellowships, cancellation of doctoral registration, and formal disciplinary proceedings before the Proctorial Board.

documents.content:
1. PURPOSE AND ADMINISTRATIVE CHARTER
This charter establishes the executive authorities, operational portfolio, administrative subunits, and contact channels of the Office of the Dean of Research and Innovation (DEPT-RES) at Demo University.

2. DEFINITION AND CONTROLLED ENTITY DISAMBIGUATION
2.1 Dean of Research (DOR): Refers strictly to the principal academic and administrative executive (ROLE-DEAN-RES) leading research governance, doctoral administration, sponsored projects, and intellectual property.
- Cross-Domain Disambiguation Note: Dean of Research (DOR under DEPT-RES) must not be confused with the Date of Registration (DOR under DEPT-ACAD / ACAD-NOT-002 semester enrollment deadline) or Department Operational Review (DOR under IQAC / IQAC-REV-003).

3. EXECUTIVE POWERS AND STATUTORY AUTHORITIES
3.1 Sponsored Grant Approvals: The Dean of Research evaluates and signs off on all competitive external funding proposals submitted to government agencies (DST, SERB, CSIR, ISRO) and corporate sponsors.
3.2 Doctoral Oversight: Authorizes the constitution of Doctoral Committees (DC), ratifies comprehensive examination outcomes, and certifies thesis evaluation panels.
3.3 Fellowship Sanction: Directs the monthly release of institutional and project research fellowships following progress reviews under REL-014.
3.4 Research Travel and Seed Funding: Sanctions institutional travel grants for faculty and scholars attending national/international conferences (FIN-POL-006) and approves internal seed funding allocations.

4. LOCATION AND ADMINISTRATIVE CONTACT
4.1 Physical Office: Faraday Tower, 4th Floor Innovation Suite.
4.2 Subunits: Sponsored Projects Cell, Doctoral Studies & Ph.D. Registry, Intellectual Property & Technology Transfer Desk, and Research Ethics Review Board.
4.3 Operating Hours: Monday through Friday, 09:00 to 17:30 IST. Support tickets and appointment requests are submitted through ResolveDesk under 'Research & Innovation'.
